set.body:
secondsPerTr = 1.5 is load-bearing and declared in three places, reconciled in none:
- docs/data/sherlock/timebase-repair.json coordinateSystems[2].secondsPerTr (silent under mutation, measured 2026-09-17)
- embed-bench/.../bench/sherlock/SherlockSceneCoding.scala:18 `val trSeconds: Double = 1.5`
- tools/recall-study/gold_scene.py:22 `TR = 1.5` (replaced from a descriptor only when configure() is called)

The alias rule (gold subject n -> participant NN0n, with a skip over the omitted source) is likewise implemented in both Scala (SherlockSceneCoding.scala) and Python (gold_scene.py, gold_subject_of). The intake evidence record states that cross-language agreement is UNPINNED: test_gold_rule_single.py compares Python to Python and never reads SherlockSceneCoding.scala.

Do: one declared source (the descriptor or the record), both implementations read it, and a test fails if Scala and Python disagree on any participant or on the TR.

Overlaps bd-01M2TA5FB4ATF9QS9ZA9MDJNE2 (Phase 1a fail-closed scorer, gold_scene.py). Coordinate; it edits the same file.
set.title: Gold rule: bind secondsPerTr and the alias rule across timebase-repair.json, SherlockSceneCoding.scala and gold_scene.py
